title: vl02: <f, g> on square-integrable functions is called an inner product, but <f, f> = 0 does not force f = 0

legacy.old_text: Auch hier gibt es ein Skalarprodukt; an die Stelle der Summe tritt ein Integral:
legacy.new_text: Regel~4 von Proposition~\ref{c03.prop.skalarprodukt} fehlt mit Absicht in dieser Liste. Dass $\braket{f}{f} = 0$ nur für $f = 0$ gilt, ist für Funktionen nicht ganz richtig, und die Reparatur steht im Fundament.

legacy.old_text: Here too there is an inner product; an integral takes the place of the sum:
legacy.new_text: Rule~4 of Proposition~\ref{c03.prop.skalarprodukt} is missing from this list on purpose. That $\braket{f}{f} = 0$ holds only for $f = 0$ is not quite right for functions, and the repair is in the Foundations.

reason: The function equal to 1 at x = 0 and 0 elsewhere is square-integrable, nonzero, and has <f, f> = 0, so <., .> is not positive definite on functions. The precise space consists of classes of functions equal almost everywhere (Reed-Simon I p. 17, p. 68). A scope omission rather than a false formula; the script also does not show that f^* g is integrable. The new chapter proves integrability (c03.prop.ltwo), withholds rule 4 in Vertiefung c03.v2 and repairs it in Fundament c03.f2 (D80, c03.eq.klassen).
